evidence.excerpt:
governed end-to-end agentic research system designed
to support scientific workflows in institutionally constrained environments. NAIS combines durable
research state, proposal-level planning, agentic execution, brokered data access, reproducible
workflow orchestration, evidence tracking, and scientist-in-the-loop oversight. Rather than granting
an agent unrestricted access to protected data, NAIS separates reasoning and orchestration from data
governance: the agent submits approved actions through controlled interfaces, protected data remain
inside institutional infrastructure, and only governed artifacts such as aggregate summaries, quality-
control metrics, plots, logs, and manuscript-oriented evidence are returned. Figure 1 illustrates
the overall architecture, showing how proposal review, agentic execution, and governed data access
compose into an end-to-end research system.

Comparison of expert reference versus NemoClaw labels revealed systematic discordance concentrated
near clinical thresholds, not random misclassification (Figure 3). Among 3,950 subjects labeled
hypertensive by NemoClaw but normotensive in the expert reference, 2,911 (73.7%) had systolic
blood pressure > 140mmHg or diastolic > 90mmHg, indicating clinically elevated measurements
despite absent ICD/medication labels in the expert track.
We requested a medication audit. NemoClaw generated SQL querying antihypertensive prescrip-
tions across angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, beta-blockers,
calcium-channel blockers, diuretics, and related classes (lisinopril through aliskiren). Only 125 of
the 3,950 discordant subjects had antihypertensive medication records, explaining much of the
disagreement: the expert cohort incorporated diagnosis and Rx history,

evidence.excerpt:
Generalizability is the primary constraint. The NAIS deployment is a single-institution case
study, and broader claims about NAIS performance require validation across additional hospital
environments and data governance frameworks.
The GWAS results are replication evidence, not novel discovery. Lead loci are identified qualitatively
from Manhattan-plot inspection. Exact per-SNP effect sizes and lead variant identification require
extraction from the underlying association result files, which was not performed for this manuscript.
The DILI prediction case remains illustrative. Model E was evaluated on 390 compounds using
5-fold Murcko scaffold cross-validation with low variance (SD 0.018), and ablation of the Diff-
Dock/thermodynamics branches drops AUC to 0.71, confirming the contribution of structural
features. A dataset of this size is insufficient for clinical-grade validation

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The claims that NAIS executes end-to-end workflows while preserving institutional privacy boundaries and generating outputs comparable to expert analyses are supported by empirical GWAS results, label confusion matrices, discordance analysis, and multi-modal predictive modeling benchmarks.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The platform is empirically evaluated on a real-world hypertension genome-wide association study using 286,422 individuals from a hospital biobank, successfully replicating established genomic loci (FGF5, ATP2B1, CNNM2, FTO, and GRB14) in alignment with an independently curated expert analysis. Additional validation demonstrates utility on a drug-induced liver injury prediction workflow (AUC 0.842) and across containerized benchmark runs.
primary.limitations: The authors transparently acknowledge that evaluation is largely focused on a single-institution deployment, GWAS results reflect locus replication rather than novel variant discovery without per-SNP effect extraction, and the secondary drug-induced liver injury study relied on a modest compound sample size.
primary.method_assessment: The system architecture clearly delineates reasoning and orchestration from data governance by routing requests through sandboxed execution, a broker API, and Kubeflow containers, ensuring no individual-level protected health information is released to the agent. The approach is documented via end-to-end operational stages, including proposal review, SQL cohort extraction, containerized execution, and iterative discordance auditing.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a rigorous, well-engineered architectural design addressing a vital open challenge in deploying autonomous/agentic AI within privacy-regulated biomedical environments. The system is validated through extensive real-world clinical data with clear controls, human-expert comparative baselines, and transparent documentation of limitations and failure recovery.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces the NVAITC AI Scientist (NAIS), a governed agentic research architecture that orchestrates biomedical workflows across protected institutional boundaries using brokered execution, durable state tracking, aggregate-only artifact retrieval, and human-in-the-loop oversight.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a rigorous, well-engineered architectural design addressing a vital open challenge in deploying autonomous/agentic AI within privacy-regulated biomedical environments. The system is validated through extensive real-world clinical data with clear controls, human-expert comparative baselines, and transparent documentation of limitations and failure recovery.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently acknowledge that evaluation is largely focused on a single-institution deployment, GWAS results reflect locus replication rather than novel variant discovery without per-SNP effect extraction, and the secondary drug-induced liver injury study relied on a modest compound sample size.
